title: `str.slice`: 0-based, negative offsets from the end
description: `str.slice(offset, length)` counts characters (code points) from 0; a negative offset counts from the end, and the part before the start is cut off (`slice(-10, 7)` of `hello` is `he`). An offset past the end gives `''`. A length of NULL takes the rest; a negative length is refused (`InvalidOperationError`, cast to `u64`).
With the offset shifted by one for positive starts, it matches Substrait's `substring` with `WRAP_FROM_END` on every probe row.
reference: `substring(s, start, length)`, 1-based, `negative_start: WRAP_FROM_END` (#209); offsets outside `[-2³², 2³²)` raise (#336).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
